title: Characterizing RKA[PRF] Membership
summary: Some related-key derivation classes admit RKA-secure PRFs while others do not; characterize exactly which classes do.

formal_statement.body: For a key space $K$, let $\Phi$ be a class of related-key derivation functions $\phi: K \to K$, and define $\mathrm{RKA}[\mathrm{PRF}]$ as the set of classes $\Phi$ for which some pseudorandom function is $\Phi$-RKA secure, with related-key queries restricted to functions $\phi \in \Phi$. Natural examples of classes outside $\mathrm{RKA}[\mathrm{PRF}]$ are known, and explicit constructions establish membership for certain specific classes, but no general characterization is available. Determine exactly which classes $\Phi$ belong to $\mathrm{RKA}[\mathrm{PRF}]$, equivalently, give necessary and sufficient conditions on $\Phi$ for the existence of a $\Phi$-RKA-secure pseudorandom function.

scope.domain: Related-key security of pseudorandom functions and the structure of admissible key-derivation classes.
parameters: Φ: the class of allowed related-key derivation functions mapping K to K
scope.unresolved_remainder: Give necessary and sufficient conditions on Φ for a Φ-RKA-secure pseudorandom function to exist.

progress.summary: The source explicitly asks which classes belong to RKA[PRF], noting natural classes outside it and explicit constructions for certain members. It reports that no general characterization is available.
